status: Bounded source review; not independently rerun; excluded from compact pitch as a quantitative valuation input.

Intel_commissioned_study.method: Signal65-provisioned AWS instances, 10 selected Terminal-Bench 2 tasks, fixed recorded responses, three runs; 8-vCPU and 64-vCPU configurations.
Intel_commissioned_study.finding: Xeon 6 m8i and Turin m8a had similar scheduled-batch compute cost at documented AWS rates; AMD consistently had lower elapsed time on 8-vCPU instances.
Intel_commissioned_study.critical_status_scope: All 81 measured 8-vCPU batches carry strict replay-harness Failed status because 3 of 10 recordings terminate mid-task. This is shared across all SKUs; Harbor exits cleanly and all scheduled trials run. It does not indicate hardware failure or every individual task failing. The baseline identifies four never-passing tasks, including those three.
Intel_commissioned_study.economic_scope: Complete-batch cost per scheduled trial, not per successfully completed task. Different aggregation narrows the featured 5.5% Intel cost advantage to 0.8%. No live inference, socket price, power, or production-fleet generalization.
Intel_commissioned_study.locators: PDF pp7–8 limitations and methods; pp12–13 scaling; final page discloses Intel commissioning.

AWS_primary_configuration_check.interpretation: Cloud-instance buyer cost comparison is meaningful at package level; equal vCPU is not equal physical cores and cannot establish normalized per-core CPU performance or chip ASP.

Vera_validation.scope: Headline 1.64x per-core comparison uses NVIDIA paired bare-metal measurements: 88 Vera versus 128 EPYC 9755 physical cores; 69 matched successful tasks. Signal65 reviewed methods and reran Vera, without an independently repeated paired x86 run. No measured power, whole-socket throughput, price or full-system TCO.
Vera_validation.interpretation: Credible limited validation; calling the headline wholly independent measured fleet economics overstates it.

Arm_study.scope: Arm commissioned the research. Approximately 1.99x modeled rack performance combines per-chip measurements with Arm-rated server power, not measured loaded-rack electricity. No Intel socket-price inference.

decision: These studies support heterogeneous workload and buyer-economics analysis, while requiring narrower language than a universal vendor ranking. Do not turn these ratios into Intel sales/margin inputs.
